text: Fixed and verified. `gin.Error`'s `Unwrap()` had a pointer receiver, so a wrapped `Error` *value* was a dead end in the error chain (`errors.Is`/`errors.As` stopped at it). It now has a value receiver, so the value form behaves exactly like the pointer form: `errors.Is(wrapped, innerErr)` and `errors.As(wrapped, &target)` both return true, and the pointer form still works.

Fixed and verified. `responseWriter.WriteHeader` logged the warning about headers already being written but then overwrote `w.status` anyway. It now returns early, so once the response has been sent `Status()` keeps reporting the status that was actually sent (200 in your example), while the client still receives 200.

Fixed and verified. A context's parameter/skipped-node slices are preallocated from the max parameter count known when the context was created. Routes registered after the first request raised that maximum, but pooled contexts kept the old (too small) capacity, so the tree silently dropped every parameter — and with a `*wild` segment it panicked with a slice-bounds error. `handleHTTPRequest` now grows those slices to the current maximum before matching, so `/test/john/smith/is/super/great` yields `name=john`, `last_name=smith`, `wild=/is/super/great` exactly as if the route had been registered up front (first request still 404).

Fixed and verified. `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` assumed the wildcard child was `children[0]`, but when a static route is registered next to a `:param` route the static child is inserted *before* the wildcard one, so it hit the "invalid node type" panic. It now tries the static children first (case-insensitively) and falls back to the wildcard child: `/PREFIX/XXX` redirects (301) to `/prefix/xxx`, and `/prefix/a/b/c` returns 404 instead of panicking.

Fixed and verified. `NegotiateFormat` compared the accepted and offered strings byte by byte up to the length of the accepted value, indexing the offered string out of range when the Accept entry was longer than the offer (`image/tiff-fx` vs `image/tiff`). The loop is now bounded by both lengths, so `image/tiff-fx` no longer matches `image/tiff` and `NegotiateFormat` returns "" (wildcards such as `image/*` still match).

Fixed and verified. `FileAttachment` interpolated the filename into the `Content-Disposition` header verbatim, so quotes/backslashes in a user-controlled name could inject extra header parameters. Backslashes and double quotes are now escaped, so `evil"; dummy="x.sh` is sent as `attachment; filename="evil\"; dummy=\"x.sh"` — a single, well-formed filename parameter. ASCII names are otherwise unchanged (non-ASCII still uses `filename*=UTF-8''`).
